findings.comment: Overhead electric line depicted on landscape plan (Sheet 31) along southern boundary and poles shown on existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) along western and northern boundaries, but no clearance dimension annotations are shown on site plan indicating horizontal sky-to-ground clearances from outside conductors to proposed buildings and structures.

applicableAreas: Proposed buildings and any building projections near overhead facilities
findings.comment: Building elevations and section views showing projections and their clearances from overhead electric conductors are not provided. Without elevation views with surveyed conductor locations and dimension lines to building overhangs, awnings, and balconies, clearance compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Buildings and elevated structures near overhead facilities
findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not included in the site plan set. Registered surveyor field measurements of overhead line heights and clearances to building features are not provided.

applicableAreas: Proposed buildings and site features throughout site
findings.comment: Section and enlarged plan views with dimension lines showing clearances from outer electric conductor to outermost edges of buildings and projections are not provided on the site plan sheets. Clearance verification requires specific dimension annotations originating from the conductor location, not the pole.

Clearance dimensions are not labeled on site plans. Where clearance dimensions are required, they must originate from the outside conductor (outer electric wire), not from utility pole centerline or pole structure. Multi-conductor installations may have conductors several feet offset from pole center, making pole-measured clearances inaccurate.

applicableAreas: Overhead electric line crossing on southern boundary near proposed landscaping and trees
findings.comment: Existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements in areas with proposed landscaping. Registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is not provided to verify that overhead lines maintain adequate clearance to future grade elevations, especially where trees are proposed directly under the line.

applicableAreas: Landscape area along southern boundary under overhead electric line
findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows five mitigation trees (designated 'M') proposed directly over or immediately adjacent to the overhead electric line on the southern boundary. Plant list (Sheet 35) specifies Cedar Elm (10 trees, mature height significantly exceeds 20 feet) and Live Oak (2 trees, mature height significantly exceeds 20 feet) as proposed shade trees. These large canopy species are NOT utility-compatible for planting within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Only utility-compatible trees with mature height ≤20 feet (such as Texas Mountain Laurel and Mexican Redbud per ECM Appendix F) are permitted within the 10-foot clearance zone. No 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designation provided for any trees.

applicableAreas: Down guy anchor point on northern property boundary
findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) depicts a down guy anchor extending from the utility pole on the northern property boundary. No easement exhibit or easement documentation is provided showing a dedicated 10-foot-wide easement extending 5 feet past where the down guy enters the ground, as required for down guy anchor points.

applicableAreas: Entire site where overhead electric facilities exist
findings.comment: No plan note is visible requiring that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines as required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. This notification requirement must appear on cover sheet or general notes with specific reference to Austin Energy.
